I want to push back one one point:  Gold is unlike all other commodities in that almost all the gold ever mined is still available for consumption.  It's either in jewelry, coins, bars, small percentages in computer chips and other electronics, etc.  Therefore, newly mined gold only adds 2% or so to the total real supply and thus is not a significant factor in the price.  ie. if the price goes to $3,000/oz, it won't bring on much more new mined supply, but will bring out a lot of old coins and bars on the market.

Even for silver, some of it is lost to landfills over time because it's not economical to recover some of it.  For copper, it's a bigger loss, for iron/steel, even more.  Oil and gas and corn is totally consumed.
